docs.title: 111 (Head Hunt) 🔪
docs.text:
Best For: Players who want maximum skill expression and speed.

Tradeoff: Unforgiving rotation with very little room for error.

  • This is the final form of the old-school Remaining Energy gameplay.
  • Head Hunt is used in the rotation, so it may not be available for recovery or counter.
  • Similar rotation to Fatal Wave builds, but lower orb generation and fewer recovery options.

NoteOptional

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
CyclesOpenersRecovery

Use an Opener, then alternate between these two cycles as needed:

1Void Strike + Deathly Slash

2Soul Absorber + Blitz Rush

Aim to fit up to Cycle 2's Twin Shadows under Cycle 1's Maelstrom to reach 3 orbs without recasting or using recovery options. If you don't, an extra Head Hunt cast is required at the end of Cycle 2.

Using Head Hunt in Cycle 2 may force you to cast it at the end of the next Cycle 1, which creates downtime.

Maelstrom management is extremely important when the rotation fails, you should cast it as it expires if needed.

Due to limited orb generation, Turning Slash's after-effects may need to carry over to the following cycle.

Openers stack Adrenaline and apply synergies efficiently. If it feels overwhelming, just apply synergy and Surge at full orbs; that's all you need to start the alternating cycles.

From 3 orbs ( Stimulant):

  • Blade Assault is interchangeable with Cycle 2 if it's available.
  • It's efficient to use Atropine after Deathly Slash, with Blade Assault available.

From zero/partial orbs:

  • Cycle 1 if Deathly Slash is available, otherwise start from Maelstrom + Cycle 2.

TipRecovery Video

Watch this 54-minute 111 recovery video or consider an easier build.

  • Use spare Twin Shadows/Maelstrom stacks and/or Blitz Rush if you miss major skills.

docs.title: 313 (High Floor) 💜
docs.text:
Best For: Players who want a simpler, faster, and more forgiving Fatal Wave build.

Tradeoff: Lower damage ceiling, but easier to recover from mistakes.

  • Head Hunt is always free for counters, recovery, purify, or Adrenaline upkeep.
  • Accessible from a 14p Star core as 113 (Arts), a transitional core-limited option.
  • Move on to 333 (Ceiling) when you're ready, or stay here if you prefer!

docs.text:
TipArk Passive
  • Use the Ark Passive Calculator to optimize Evolution nodes.
  • Release Potential 3 / Instant Spell 3 / Awakening Amplifier 1 can solve mana issues at a minor DPS loss.

Alt113 (Arts) core-limited

docs.title: Skill Setup
docs.text:
TipRunes
  • Use Legendary Galewind, Purify or green Wealth on Head Hunt if you have no mana issues.
  • Legendary Focus on Maelstrom can solve major mana issues at a minor loss of orb generation.
NoteOptional
  • You can bring Head Hunt down to Lv 1 and Void Strike up to Lv 14 for +0.5% DPS and lower mana use.
    • However, Lv 7 is more practical and makes recovery much easier and faster. ★
    • At Lv 7, Magick Control tripod can help solve mana issues if you don't need the CDR.
    • Lv 4 Head Hunt (Quick Prep) with Void Strike Lv 13 is a decent overall compromise.
WarnBalance Patch
  • Swift Fingers may become the default 1st row tripod for Blitz Rush.
    • ~2% DPS loss but CPM and playability increases may make up for it.
    • Void Strike is raised to Lv 13 and Blitz Rush is lowered to Lv 12.
    • Gem priority of Void Strike and Blitz Rush is swapped.
  • Needs live testing, 313 is so fast that it might not benefit fully.
  • See Essentials for class-wide changes.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
CyclesOpenersRecoveryTL;DR:

Use an Opener, then alternate between these two cycles as needed:

1Void Strike + Deathly Slash

2Soul Absorber + Blitz Rush

Aim to fit up to Cycle 2's Twin Shadows under Cycle 1's Maelstrom to reach 3 orbs without recasting or using recovery options. If you only landed up to Soul Absorber, an extra Head Hunt cast is usually enough.

The Maelstrom in Cycle 2 is only cast if you'd otherwise miss 3 orbs. Use your judgment. If cast, it lasts at least until Cycle 1's Void Strike; recasting it as it expires aligns cooldowns. If it wasn't needed or it didn't last, nothing changes.

Openers stack Adrenaline and apply synergies efficiently. If it feels overwhelming, just apply synergy and Surge at full orbs; that's all you need to start the alternating cycles.

From 3 orbs ( Stimulant):

  • Blade Assault is interchangeable with Cycle 2 if it's available.
  • It's efficient to use Atropine after Deathly Slash, with Blade Assault available.

From zero/partial orbs:

  • Cycle 1 if Deathly Slash is available, otherwise start from Maelstrom + Cycle 2.
  • Prioritize Turning Slash earlier for synergy and Deathly Slash last for Adrenaline/RE buff.

TipRecovery Video

Watch this 2-minute 333 recovery video and read the segment titles.

  • 313 plays similarly, just Turning Slash → Fatal Wave instead of FTF.
  • Use Head Hunt when a little short on orbs, just cast if unsure.
  • Use spare Twin Shadows/Maelstrom stacks and/or Blitz Rush if you miss major skills.
  • Use Head Hunt instead of Twin Shadows for a cycle to recover stacks if they run out.
  • Use Maelstrom + Fatal Wave earlier if waiting on main orb generation skills.

docs.title: 333 (Ceiling) ✨
docs.text:
Best For: Players who want the highest damage RE build.

Tradeoff: Slightly lower orb generation and a less forgiving rotation.

  • Uses Fatal Wave as two fast casts (FTF combo) via a skill reset.
  • Head Hunt is always free for counters, recovery, purify, or Adrenaline upkeep.
  • High gem efficiency, Fatal Wave and Deathly Slash are most of your DPS.
  • Susceptible to high ping or low FPS, but you can compensate with a few changes.

Mana food and Atk/Move Speed feast are required to play Ark Grid Remaining Energy optimally.

Where Change Evolution Ark Raise Illicit Spell instead of Limit Break (unimportant content only) Leap Ark Release Potential 3 / Instant Spell 3 / Awakening Amplifier 1 ★ Head Hunt Magick Control tripod, Focus rune, or set to Lv 1 (Fatal Wave only) Maelstrom Focus rune (easier builds with excess orb generation only) TipQuick Tips
  • Optimize Ark Passive nodes or compare bracelet lines here!

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
• Orb Generation: Skills generate Death Orbs when they hit.
  • Surge: Press [Z] with 1+ orbs to consume them and activate the skill.
  • 3 Orbs: Aim to always Surge with 3 orbs for the strongest buffs and cooldown reduction.

docs.title: Identity Buffs
docs.text:
• +12% Attack Speed.
  • +12% Move Speed.
  • Attack Power based on orbs consumed.
  • Cooldown Reduction and Mana Restoration based on orbs consumed.

The cooldown reduction is the core of the class: the cycle resets so you can start generating your next set of orbs.

docs.title: Party Synergies
docs.text:
• Turning Slash: +4% outgoing and +5% directional damage for 12s.
  • Maelstrom: +12.8% Attack/Move Speed for 6s and improves orb generation.

docs.title: Playstyle
docs.text:
Remaining Energy is a continuous cycle:

Generate Orbs → 3 Orbs → Surge → Repeat.

Prioritize consistent uptime and good use of Maelstrom's buffs over back attacks. Use Surge to reposition.

docs.title: Combat Performance
docs.text:
Surge Casts Per Minute (CPM) is a useful measure of how efficiently you are playing and generating orbs.

Only compare CPM between the same encounter and build, as boss uptime and mechanics heavily affect it.

docs.title: FPS/Latency
docs.text:
• Higher FPS increases CPM and helps fit skills under Maelstrom buff.
  • High latency or low FPS hinders skill queuing and can cause 2.9 orbs.
  • Graphics settings on Low/OFF and forced 21:9 can increase FPS in some cases.
  • Join lobbies closer to your region or avoid builds with very tight orb generation.

docs.title: Standard 🌱
docs.text:
Best For: Brand-new Remaining Energy players with no Ark Grid yet.

Tradeoff: Legacy build with some downtime and little to no recovery.

  • Last bastion of the classic Remaining Energy gameplay, now powercrept.
  • Counter is used in rotation often, you must hold it when necessary.
  • Simple to learn and execute, with better mobility than modern builds.
Build Profile

Video Guide Gameplay

NoteAbout This Build

Since this is a beginner legacy build, this guide strays slightly from the norm to offer a smoother experience without deep min-maxing. For instance, you won't need mana food or stimulants to enjoy the gameplay.

New to Deathblade entirely? Surge is generally more beginner-friendly and outperforms RE Standard.

docs.title: Rotation
docs.text:
Cast Spincutter to approach the boss, use the opener and continue to loop the main cycle afterwards.

The opener stacks Adrenaline and applies synergies efficiently as you build up to the encounter's first Surge.

Opener from zero orbs:

Main repeating cycle:

  • Deathly Slash is only available every other rotation, just keep going if it's on cooldown.
  • Use Spincutter during downtime to reposition, or hold it to dodge upcoming attacks.
  • Use Blade Assault for damage, or hold it for Hyper Awakening or a clutch recovery.
  • The rotation is bottle-necked entirely by Soul Absorber's cooldown, it is what it is.
    • You can skip Earth Cleaver if Soul Absorber's off cooldown already.

Recovery:

  • Use spare Twin Shadows or Maelstrom stacks to recover if it'll help you reach 3 orbs.
    • If not, just AFK or Surge with 2 orbs and AFK. Welcome to Standard Remaining Energy.

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
• Orb Generation: Normal skills generate Death Orbs when they hit.
  • Death Trance: Press [Z] with 1+ orbs to enter Death Trance.
  • Stack Generation: Skills generate Surge stacks while in Death Trance.
  • Stack Cap: You can hold up to 80 stacks.
  • Surge: Press [Z] to consume 60 stacks. Extra stacks roll over to the next cycle.
  • Stack Requirement: Surge must be cast with 40+ stacks to refund all 3 Death Orbs.

docs.title: Death Trance Buffs
docs.text:
• 10/15/20% Attack Speed.
  • 10% Move Speed.
  • 8/16/24% Attack Power.
  • 15/25/45% Mana Restoration.
  • 10/30/50% Cooldown Reduction.

Aim to enter Death Trance with 3 orbs whenever possible.

docs.title: Party Synergies
docs.text:
• Turning Slash: +4% outgoing and +5% directional damage for 12s.
  • Surprise Attack: +4% outgoing and +5% directional damage for 6s.
  • Maelstrom: +12.8% Attack/Move Speed for 6s.

docs.title: Playstyle
docs.text:
Surge is a repeating cycle:

3 Orbs → Death Trance → Build Stacks → Surge → Repeat.

Build toward 60 stacks using your multi-hit skills, then land Surge as a Back Attack.

The 80-stack cap and rollover give you flexibility. You don't need to stop or force a skill just to hit exactly 60.

Knowing roughly how many stacks each skill generates is important for adapting your rotation.

docs.title: Combat Performance
docs.text:
Surge Casts Per Minute (CPM) and back attack rate are useful measures of how efficiently you cycle Surge.

Only compare CPM between the same encounter and build, as boss uptime and mechanics heavily affect it.
